title: Best Lightweight Strollers UK
short: Seven compact, cabin-friendly strollers tested by parents over weeks, compared on fold, weight, comfort and how well they travel.
intro: A lightweight stroller trades some of a full travel system's bulk for portability, and the best ones still fold in seconds and fit in an overhead locker. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated September 2026), which combined Which? test data with weeks of hands-on testing by parents and their children in everyday situations: school runs, city streets, holidays and public transport, assessing folding, portability, comfort, manoeuvrability, storage and value. Prices shown are RRPs quoted by Mumsnet.

products.name: YOYO³
products.best_for: Parents who want a compact stroller from birth that lasts to four years and flies as cabin luggage
products.key_spec: Birth (with newborn pack) to 4 years, 6.2kg, 10kg basket, meets most airlines' cabin luggage dimensions, multi-position recline
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy. Tester Jilly found manoeuvrability one of its strongest features, with small nimble wheels fitting through tight spaces and effortless one-handed steering. It has reflective wheel rings, a basket that now holds up to 10kg, improved suspension and more breathable mesh on the straps and backrest. The white wheels show up dirt easily, a rain cover is sold separately, and it needs some assembly.
pros: Easy to collapse and carry, with cover bag and strap included
Meets cabin luggage dimensions of most airlines
cons: White wheels show up dirt easily
Requires some assembly, and is expensive

products.name: Aries Autofold Stroller
products.best_for: Parents who want the easiest possible fold at a low price
products.key_spec: Birth to about 5 years, 6.1kg, auto-fold at the press of two buttons, multi-position recline, rain cover and bumper bar included
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Claire, a mum of two, said it's by far the easiest stroller she's ever folded and lifted into a car boot. It's ultra-lightweight with a small footprint, and different bundle versions add a foot warmer, cup holder or organiser. Claire liked the hood's back pocket for extra storage and found the seat comfortable for both her one-year-old and two-and-a-half-year-old. Fabrics aren't machine-washable and the handlebar isn't adjustable.
pros: Multi-position recline and good storage space
Comes with rain cover and bumper bar

products.name: Clic 2
products.best_for: Newborns who need to lie fully flat for naps on the go
products.key_spec: Birth to 4 years, 6.5kg, full lie-flat seat, lockable swivel wheels, carry-strap fold, not car seat compatible
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Tamsin used it for a month and was impressed by how easy it was to lift, carry and fold thanks to the carry-strap mechanism, ideal for public transport. At 6.5kg it's one of the lightest strollers tested, and its full lie-flat seat suited her five-month-old's naps. It handles pavements and smooth surfaces well but isn't built for rough terrain, isn't cabin-approved (unlike the Silver Cross Jet 5), and the handlebar isn't adjustable.
pros: Super lightweight with lockable swivel wheels
Large sun canopy and easy to carry
Comes with a rain cover and bumper bar
cons: Not cabin-approved, so needs to be checked in

products.name: Aer²
products.best_for: Parents who want a one-handed fold and a genuinely foldable overnight-sleep carrycot
products.key_spec: Birth to 4 years (22kg), 6.5kg, one-second one-hand fold, full lie-flat recline, 8kg basket, 10-year warranty
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Sophie was surprised how light it felt given how sturdy it looks and feels compared with other lightweight strollers. Its one-second, one-hand fold collapses into a self-standing position for cabin-approved travel, and it has the world's first fully foldable carrycot, also approved for overnight sleep. It's made from recycled PET bottles with a 10-year transferable warranty. The only drawback Mumsnet notes is the premium price.
pros: Extra-long seat, ideal for taller children

products.name: Orfeo
products.best_for: Daily use that still needs a genuinely cabin-approved fold
products.key_spec: Birth to about 4 years, 6.3kg, cabin-approved fold, 5kg under-seat basket, near-flat recline, car seat compatible
products.summary: Winner of a Red Dot Design Award. Mumsnet's tester Lily used it daily with her two-year-old and awarded it a full five stars, praising the enhanced suspension, sturdy wheels, smooth handling and near-flat recline that lowers gently without jolting a sleeping child. A fixed handlebar was still comfortable for her 6ft 2in husband. It's forward-facing only unless used with a car seat, and has no bumper bar.
pros: Small footprint when unfolded, generous basket
Harness is easy to adjust, no rethreading
cons: Forward-facing only unless used with a car seat

products.name: Pip
products.best_for: City living and frequent trips where a compact, one-handed-open stroller matters
products.key_spec: Birth to 4 years, 7kg, IATA cabin-approved, lie-flat recline, extra-large UPF50+ canopy
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Laura used it for eight weeks with her eight-month-old and found it effortless day to day: 'It's light, sleek and easy to carry,' adding that opening it one-handed while holding her child was a game changer. It's cabin-approved and small enough for an overhead locker or car boot. The handlebar isn't adjustable and the rain cover doesn't offer full coverage.
cons: Rain cover doesn't offer full coverage

products.name: Libelle
products.best_for: Holidays and flights where the stroller must fold to carry-on size
products.key_spec: 6 months to 4 years (birth with a compatible car seat), 5.9kg, folds to 48 x 32 x 20cm, stands unaided, pre-assembled
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Matt found it folds down to the size of a small carry-on suitcase, one of the lightest strollers tested, and it stands up on its own with side carry handles. Colour-coded buttons make folding easy and it comes pre-assembled. The small wheels struggled on rough terrain like grass, the three-point harness slipped with a bouncing toddler, a changing bag was hard to fit in the 5kg basket, and there's no belly bar included.

specs.Age range: 6 months to 4 years (birth with compatible car seat)

pros: Folds to the size of a small suitcase
Stands up when folded, with carry handles
Infinite recline, no assembly needed, cabin-approved
cons: Wheels struggled on rough terrain such as grass
No bumper bar included, and mud settles into the fabric if not wiped quickly

guide.q: Which stroller is best for flying?
guide.a: The Cybex Libelle folds to carry-on suitcase size and stands on its own, making it Mumsnet's pick for frequent flyers. The Stokke YOYO³, Joolz Aer², Cybex Orfeo and iCandy Pip are also cabin-approved, while the Silver Cross Clic 2 is not and will usually need checking in.

guide.q: Can a lightweight stroller be used from birth?
guide.a: Several fully recline flat: the Silver Cross Clic 2, Joolz Aer², Stokke YOYO³ (with the newborn pack) and iCandy Pip all lie flat for newborn naps. The Cybex Libelle is rated from six months unless paired with a compatible infant car seat.

guide.q: How much does weight matter day to day?
guide.a: For carrying up stairs or onto buses, every kilogram counts. The Cybex Libelle (5.9kg), Ickle Bubba Aries (6.1kg) and Stokke YOYO³ (6.2kg) are the lightest here, while the iCandy Pip (7kg) is still light but slightly heavier for its extra features.

guide.q: Will it cope with anything other than pavements?
guide.a: Not really. Mumsnet's testers found the small wheels on lightweight strollers, including the Cybex Libelle, struggle on grass and rough ground. These are designed for pavements, city life and travel; for countryside walks Mumsnet suggests a proper all-terrain pram instead.
